note: A cleft sentence splits an ordinary statement into two parts specifically to spotlight one element — genuinely new C1 stylistic territory, not just another connector.

examples.de: Spaltsätze lenken die Aufmerksamkeit gezielt auf ein einzelnes Satzglied.
examples.en: Cleft sentences deliberately direct attention to a single sentence element.

note: Splits a plain statement in two: es + sein + the focused element, then a relative clause carrying the rest of the content. The es is a pure placeholder, not the real subject.

examples.de: Es war die Finanzkrise, die den Ausschlag gab.
examples.en: It was the financial crisis that tipped the balance.

note: The plural version — sein agrees with the focused plural noun, not with the dummy es.

examples.de: Es sind vor allem die jungen Wähler, die den Unterschied gemacht haben.
examples.en: It's mainly the young voters who made the difference.

note: Fronts a topic before commenting on it — often resumed with "so" at the start of the main clause.

examples.de: Was die Kosten betrifft, so sind sie überschaubar.
examples.en: As for the costs, they are manageable.

english: as for X, as far as X is concerned
note: A near-synonym of was X betrifft — interchangeable in most contexts, slightly more personal in feel.

examples.de: Was die Sicherheit angeht, gibt es noch offene Fragen.
examples.en: As for safety, there are still open questions.

note: A was-cleft: a free relative clause (built the same way as B1's was …, das …) fronts the point of emphasis, then ist introduces what it amounts to.

examples.de: Was mich überrascht, ist die Geschwindigkeit der Entwicklung.
examples.en: What surprises me is the speed of the development.

english: word order in a cleft sentence
note: es + finite sein + the focused element + a relative clause (der/die/das/was) carrying everything else — a fixed template, however long the relative clause gets.

examples.de: Es waren die Verbraucher, die den Wandel erzwangen.
examples.en: It was the consumers who forced the change.

note: The es in Es ist X, der … isn't the real subject — it exists purely to spotlight X. Mentally skip it and read "X ist es, der/die/das …" to find the actual point being made.

examples.de: Nicht der Preis, sondern die Qualität ist es, die zählt.
examples.en: It isn't the price but the quality that counts.

english: by no means, not at all
note: A stronger, more formal denial than plain nicht — flatly rejects a suggestion or assumption.

examples.de: Das Ergebnis ist keineswegs überraschend.
examples.en: The result is by no means surprising.

note: Adds an even more extreme case after a negative statement — implies the second thing is even less likely than the first.

examples.de: Er kann nicht einmal kochen, geschweige denn backen.
examples.en: He can't even cook, let alone bake.

english: all the more (so) / even less so
note: A defiant intensifier — often the payoff after a concessive clause, signalling that an obstacle only strengthened the outcome.

examples.de: Nach der Kritik arbeitete sie erst recht hart weiter.
examples.en: After the criticism, she worked all the harder.

note: A literary, fairly rare intensifier — mainly paired with unmöglich or unvorstellbar for maximum emphasis.

examples.de: Das ist schlechterdings unmöglich.
examples.en: That is simply impossible.

note: Marks what follows as a surprising or ironic focal point — often placed right before the element it's spotlighting.

examples.de: Ausgerechnet er sollte die Rede halten.
examples.en: He, of all people, was supposed to give the speech.

note: Sets an upper limit on a claim, often minimising it — close to höchstens.

examples.de: Das kostet allenfalls hundert Euro.
examples.en: That costs at most a hundred euros.

note: The main point of weight in a text, project, or study — der Schwerpunkt liegt auf + Dativ.

examples.de: Der Schwerpunkt der Studie liegt auf der Jugendarbeitslosigkeit.
examples.en: The focus of the study is on youth unemployment.

note: A more formal synonym of Schwerpunkt — literally "main eye-mark" — das Hauptaugenmerk liegt auf + Dativ. No natural plural.

examples.de: Das Hauptaugenmerk liegt auf der Sicherheit.
examples.en: The main focus is on safety.

note: Something of secondary importance — the opposite of a Schwerpunkt.

examples.de: Das Geld ist für sie Nebensache.
examples.en: Money is a minor matter for her.

note: A remark added almost as an afterthought — nur als Randbemerkung.

examples.de: Das nur als Randbemerkung.
examples.en: That's just a side note.

note: How much relative importance is assigned to different factors — die Gewichtung der Kriterien.

examples.de: Die Gewichtung der Kriterien wurde verändert.
examples.en: The weighting of the criteria was changed.

note: Describes what should be dealt with first, before other concerns.

examples.de: Vorrangig geht es um die Sicherheit.
examples.en: The primary concern is safety.

note: The adjective matching Nebensache — worth mentioning, but not the point.

examples.de: Der Preis ist hier nebensächlich.
examples.en: The price is secondary here.

note: The formal noun for what comes first — oberste Priorität haben, Prioritäten setzen.

examples.de: Sicherheit hat oberste Priorität.
examples.en: Safety is the top priority.

note: Describes what appears to be the point at first glance — often set up to be contradicted by a deeper reality.

examples.de: Vordergründig geht es um Sparmaßnahmen, tatsächlich aber um Machtpolitik.
examples.en: On the surface it's about austerity measures, but it's actually about power politics.

note: How much something matters to the point at hand — von großer/geringer Relevanz. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Relevanz dieser Frage wird oft unterschätzt.
examples.en: The relevance of this question is often underestimated.

note: Describes something that doesn't matter for the decision or argument at hand.

examples.de: Das ist für die Entscheidung irrelevant.
examples.en: That's irrelevant to the decision.

note: Close to irrelevant, but leans more toward "not worth mentioning" than "doesn't apply here."

examples.de: Die Details sind hier belanglos.
examples.en: The details are insignificant here.

note: A firm, formal refusal or exclusion — stronger than nicht, close to keineswegs but more about ruling out a future possibility.

examples.de: Das darf keinesfalls passieren.
examples.en: That must not happen under any circumstances.

note: Affirms something, often countering an expected doubt — durchaus möglich, durchaus üblich.

examples.de: Das ist durchaus möglich.
examples.en: That is quite possible.
